title: Hydraulic Brake Actuation: Diagnostic Starting Point
introduction:
Hydraulic brake actuation carries your pedal input to the calipers as pressure. The master cylinder develops that pressure, and the caliper pistons use it to press the pads against the discs. Think of pressure as the system's shared language: the pedal starts the conversation, and the calipers turn it into clamping force.

I first separate a pedal-feel concern from noise, pulling, drag or vibration and describe when it occurs. Those observations help frame diagnosis; they do not prove a hydraulic fault. Continue through the required brake-system diagnostic referral below. This page does not contain the equipment, test setup, measurements or result branches needed for a standalone diagnostic procedure.

edits.text: For hydraulic brake actuation diagnosis, refer to Brake System (206-00 Brake System - General Information, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: Pedal input, hydraulic pressure and pad application are connected, but each has a different role. The diagnostic referral is needed to determine which checks fit the concern instead of treating every braking symptom as a hydraulic failure.
